profiles.welcome: Learn to code by building your own game!

home.basicsIntro: Learn the building blocks of code with Bit the robot.
home.gamesIntro: Pick a game and build it step by step.

lesson.useArrows: Use the arrow keys on your keyboard!

msg.noKeys: Add "when key … is pressed" blocks so you can steer.

err.string: This text has no closing {q}. Text must start and end with {q}.
err.comment: This /* comment */ is never closed with */.
err.extraClose: There is one {ch} too many here.
err.mismatch: Here is a {close}, but the {open} on line {openLine} needs a {want} first.
err.unclosed: This {open} is never closed. Add a {close} where it should end.

err.eventName: "{name}" should be written {want}. Capital letters matter!
err.syntax: The computer doesn't understand this line. Check for typos. ({detail})
err.notDefined: "{name}" doesn't exist. Check the spelling: capital letters matter!

code.symbolsTip: Click on any symbol or word in your code to see what it means there.

explain.idle: Click on any symbol or word in your code, and I'll tell you what it means.
explain.comment: // starts a comment: a note for people reading the code. The computer skips everything after // on that line.
explain.string: {text} is text. The quotes ' ' show where the text starts and ends, so the computer knows it's a word to use, not a command.
explain.number: {n} is a number. You can change it.
explain.semicolon: ; ends a command, like a full stop ends a sentence.
explain.semicolonFor: Inside for ( ), the ; splits the three parts: where the counter starts, how long to keep going, and how the counter changes.
explain.brace: { } curly brackets hold a group of code that belongs together.
explain.braceEvent: { } hold the code of {name}. Everything between { and } runs when that happens.
explain.braceFunction: { } hold the code of the function {name}. It runs every time you write {name}().
explain.braceIf: { } hold the code that only runs if the question in if ( ) is true.
explain.braceElse: { } hold the code that runs when the if question is NOT true.
explain.braceLoop: { } hold the code the loop repeats. Everything between { and } runs again each time round.
explain.paren: ( ) round brackets group things together, like in maths.
explain.parenIf: ( ) after if hold a question. The code in { } only runs if the answer is yes (true).
explain.parenFor: ( ) after for hold three parts, split by ; : where the counter starts, how long to keep going, and how the counter changes each time.
explain.parenWhile: ( ) after while hold a question. The loop keeps going as long as the answer is yes (true).
explain.parenFunction: ( ) after {name}: here a function can ask for extra information. Empty ( ) means it needs none.
explain.parenCall: ( ) after {name} make the command run. What's inside is extra information for it, like which way to go.
explain.parenCallEmpty: ( ) after {name} make the command run. It needs no extra information, but you still need the ( ), or it won't run!
explain.dot: The dot means "belongs to". bit.move is the move command that belongs to Bit.
explain.comma: A comma separates things in a list.
explain.assign: = puts a value into a variable. let i = 0 means: make a box called i and put 0 in it. (To ask "are they the same?" you use ===.)
explain.less: < means "less than". i < 4 is true while i is 0, 1, 2 or 3.
explain.greater: > means "more than". score > 5 is true when the score is 6 or more.
explain.lessEq: <= means "less than or the same as".
explain.greaterEq: >= means "more than or the same as".
explain.equals: {op} asks: are these two the same? The answer is true or false.
explain.notEquals: {op} asks: are these two different? The answer is true or false.
explain.plusPlus: ++ adds 1. i++ is a short way to write i = i + 1.
explain.minusMinus: -- takes away 1. i-- is a short way to write i = i - 1.
explain.plus: + adds numbers together (or joins text together).
explain.minus: - takes one number away from another.
explain.remainder: % gives what's left over after dividing: 7 % 3 is 1.
explain.not: ! means "not". It turns true into false, and false into true.
explain.and: && means "and": both sides must be true.
explain.or: || means "or": one side being true is enough.
explain.squareBrackets: [ ] square brackets make a list, or pick one thing out of a list.
explain.plusEquals: += adds to a variable. score += 2 is short for score = score + 2.
explain.minusEquals: -= takes away from a variable. lives -= 1 is short for lives = lives - 1.
explain.arrow: => makes a short function: what comes before it is the input, and after it is what the function does.
explain.colon: : separates a name from its value.
explain.function: function makes a named piece of code. Its code goes between { and }.
explain.for: for is a loop: it repeats the code in { }. The ( ) say how many times.
explain.while: while is a loop: it repeats the code in { } as long as the question in ( ) is true.
explain.do: do starts a loop that runs the code in { } first, and asks the while question after.
explain.if: if lets the code choose: the code in { } only runs if the question in ( ) is true.
explain.else: else means "otherwise": its { } code runs when the if question is not true.
explain.let: let makes a new variable: a box with a name that remembers a value, like a score.
explain.const: const makes a box with a name whose value never changes.
explain.return: return ends the function and gives back a value.
explain.true: true means yes. Questions like bit.isOnCoin() answer true or false.
explain.false: false means no. Questions like bit.isOnCoin() answer true or false.
explain.break: break stops the loop straight away.
explain.continue: continue skips the rest of this time round the loop and starts the next one.
explain.event_start: {name} is a special name: its code runs once, when you press ▶ Run. Capital letters matter!
explain.event_tick: {name} is a special name: its code runs again and again, many times every second, while the game is on.
explain.event_key: {name} is a special name: its code runs every time the {key} arrow key is pressed.
explain.bit: bit is Bit the robot. Write a dot after it to use one of Bit's commands, like bit.move.
explain.snake: snake is your snake. Write a dot after it to use one of its commands, like snake.move.
explain.game: game is the game itself: the score, game over and speed. Write a dot after it, like game.changeScore.
explain.console: console is the box under your code. console.log writes a message in it.
explain.math: Math has maths helpers, like Math.random() for a random number.
explain.memberUnknown: There is no command called {name}. Look in the Commands list for what {obj} can do.
explain.ownFunction: {name} is the name of a function you made. Use it by writing {name}();
explain.counter: {name} is the loop's counter. It counts 0, 1, 2, … one more each time round the loop.
explain.newVariable: {name} is a new variable: a box with a name that remembers a value.
explain.name: {name} is a name, for example a variable you made. If you meant a command, check the spelling: capital letters matter!

glossary.braces: hold a group of code that belongs together: the code of a function, a loop or an if
glossary.parens: after a command: make it run, with extra info inside. After if, for, while: hold the question
glossary.quotes: show where text starts and ends: 'right' is a word, not a command
glossary.semicolon: ends a command, like a full stop
glossary.dot: "belongs to": bit.move is Bit's move command
glossary.assign: puts a value in a variable: let i = 0
glossary.compare: less than and more than: i < 4
glossary.comment: a note for people; the computer skips it
